content:
The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu will visit Chhattisgarh from October 22 to 23, 2026.

On October 23, the President will attend Muriya Darbar and grace a public programme on the occasion of Bastar Dussehra at Jagdalpur.

title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA PRESENTS LALIT KALA AKADEMI AWARDS TO SELECTED ARTISTS OF THE 65TH NATIONAL EXHIBITION OF ART
subtitle: LET US PROVIDE AMPLE OPPORTUNITIES TO YOUNG AND EMERGING ARTISTS TO DEVELOP THEIR TALENT, EXPLORE NEW MEDIUMS, AND EXPAND THEIR CREATIVE POTENTIAL: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 OCT 2026 3:08PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu presented Lalit Kala Akademi awards to selected artists of the 65th National Exhibition of Art in New Delhi today (October 21, 2026). She also felicitated Grand Prize winners and Honourable Mentions of the 3rd Print Biennale India, 2026.
Speaking on the occasion, the President said that this award presentation ceremony is a celebration of India’s artistic heritage, cultural diversity, and contemporary creativity. Through this event, we are celebrating the rich tradition of India’s diverse arts, its creative energy, and its ever-evolving artistic expressions.
The President said that art is not limited to paintings on a canvas, sculptures carved from stone, or works created through various other mediums. Art is a reflection of our culture. It reflects the memories, experiences of the present, and aspirations for the future. Art enables us to perceive and understand our times and society from a fresh perspective. She emphasised the need to equip traditional artists in remote areas with training in new technologies and contemporary art techniques, enabling them to showcase their skills and participate in competitions on a wider platform.
The President said that in today’s world, artists require not only creative opportunities but also financial support, access to a broader market, and connections with art collectors. She was happy to note that the Lalit Kala Akademi and the Ministry of Culture are making efforts to encourage the sale of artworks.
The President said that art should not be confined to art galleries. It should reach schools, universities, public spaces, and broader segments of society. She urged all stakeholders to provide ample op
portunities to young and emerging artists to develop their talent, explore new mediums, and expand their creative potential.

content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today expressed deep sadness over the passing of Thiru Vummidi Ethiraj Ji, who will always be remembered for his efforts in crafting the historic Sengol that was presented to former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.
Recalling the honour of meeting him in 2023 when the government gave the Sengol a place of pride in the new Parliament building, Shri Modi stated that his life and craftsmanship represent a remarkable connection between India's glorious traditions and the national journey, and extended his heartfelt condolences to his family and admirers.
In a post on X, the Prime Minister shared:
"Deeply saddened by the passing of Thiru Vummidi Ethiraj Ji. Hailing from a distinguished family based in Tamil Nadu, he will always be remembered for his efforts in crafting the historic Sengol that was presented to Former Prime Minister Nehru. title: “Solar panels above, thriving crops below”: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan inaugurates the 7th AgriVoltaics World Conference at Bharat Mandapam
subtitle:
“Farmers as both food providers and energy producers: Integrating agriculture with solar power will increase farmers’ incomes”:  Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

“AgriVoltaics policy must be designed with the interests of 85 per cent of small and marginal farmers at its core”: Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh

“Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India is leading the world in clean energy alongside its overflowing foodgrain reserves”: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

“Agriculture and Energy Ministries will work hand in hand: New employment opportunities for rural youth in their own villages”: Shri Shivraj Singh

“Non-fossil energy capacity exceeds 308 GW; AgriVoltaics can meet India’s electricity demand by 2050”: Shri Pralhad Joshi

“World’s largest AgriVoltaics campaign to be launched in the next phase of PM-KUSUM”: Union Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 OCT 2026 7:56PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan has said that under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Indian farmers are set to become not merely ‘annadatas’ (food providers), but, by adopting solar energy, will truly emerge as both ‘annadatas and urjadatas’ (food and energy providers). Addressing the inaugural session of the three-day 7th AgriVoltaics World Conference as the keynote speaker at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on Wednesday, Shri Chouhan said that integrating agriculture with solar energy was opening up a new pathway towards global welfare and greater economic prosperity for farmers. He stressed that the AgriVoltaics policy must be designed to work effectively on the fields of the country’s 85 per cent small and marginal farmers, ensuring that the benefits of this technology reached those who needed them most.
Welcoming delegates from India and abroad, along with the large number of farmers who had gathered at the venue, Union Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan explained that AgriVoltaics technology would enable solar panels to generate electricity above the ground while crops continued to flourish beneath them. Explaining the concept in simple, familiar terms, he described it as a model that delivers the best of both worlds, invoking the Hindi expressions ‘aam ke aam aur guthliyon ke daam’ and ‘hing lage na fitkari, rang bhi chokha’ to illustrate the multiple benefits of using the same land for agriculture and energy generation. He observed that while the traditional saying was ‘Rahiman paani raakhiye’ (preserve water), the needs of the modern age called for ‘Rahiman bijli raakhiye’ (preserve electricity), because modern life and agriculture would come to a standstill without power. Integrating energy production with farming, he said, was therefore one of the most important steps that could be taken in the interests of farmers.
Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Chouhan proudly highlighted India’s transformation from a country dependent on foodgrain imports to meet its food security requirements to one whose granaries were now overflowing with wheat and rice, thanks to the hard work and dedication of its farmers. Indian agriculture continues to maintain a robust growth rate of 4.5 per cent, which is a significant achievement in itself. Exports of agricultural products have reached a new record of US$52.55 billion, while sowing for the 2026–27 rabi season has recently commenced, with particular emphasis on pulses and oilseeds. He noted that these achievements reflected the progress made by Indian agriculture and underscored the importance of developing new approaches to sustain farmers’ prosperity while meeting the country’s evolving needs.
Presenting the realities on the ground before scientists and policymakers, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan pointed out that India’s average landholding was just 0.96 hectares and that more than 85 per cent of farmers were small and marginal farmers. Such farmers did not have enough land to abandon cultivation and install solar power plants exclusively on their holdings. He emphasised that while laboratories and government institutions could receive funding for experiments, farmers had to invest their hard-earned money. Therefore, the model must be practically viable on small farmers’ fields, and agricultural production must not be disrupted under any circumstances. He said the objective could not be achieved merely by planting a few crops beneath solar panels. Instead, the height of the panels, the distance between supporting structures and the arrangements for ploughing must be carefully designed to allow farmers to cultivate their land efficiently. The system should also enable them to choose different crops and change their crop cycles according to their preferences every year, without compromising agricultural productivity.
Emphasising the need to address practical challenges before projects were implemented, Shri Chouhan said that robust arrangements must be made for the safe drainage and collection of rainwater falling from solar panels. This would prevent soil erosion in agricultural fields and ensure that every drop of water was put to productive use. He also called for reliable arrangements for purchasing the electricity generated, connecting projects to the power grid and ensuring transparent and timely payments to farmers. He suggested that Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) should be actively involved in the initiative and that local rural youth and women should receive training in operating, repairing and maintaining the equipment. This would create substantial employment opportunities within villages themselves. He further made it clear that appropriate safeguards and responsibilities must be established from the outset to ensure that farmers did not bear any financial or physical burden if a company abandoned a project midway or if solar panels had to be removed upon the expiry of a contract. The interests of farmers, he stressed, must remain protected throughout the project’s lifecycle.
Shri Chouhan expressed his appreciation for the leadership of Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy Shri Pralhad Joshi and assured him that the Ministry of Agriculture would work hand in hand and shoulder to shoulder with the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy to ensure the success of this initiative. He emphasised that close coordination between the two ministries would be essential to develop a model that simultaneously supports agricultural production, promotes renewable energy and improves farmers’ economic well-being.
On the occasion, Union Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution and New and Renewable Energy, Shri Pralhad Joshi, said that the seventh edition of the conference was the largest and most historic of the international conferences held so far. Record participation had necessitated arrangements for additional halls to accommodate the attendees. He noted that, at a time when countries across the world were facing economic challenges, India continued to be the world’s fastest-growing major economy, recording GDP growth of 7.8 per cent in the first quarter of the current financial year. Shri Joshi stated that India’s total electricity generation capacity, which stood at approximately 249 GW before 2014, had now increased to more than 560 GW. Of this, installed non-fossil energy capacity had crossed 308 GW, with 100 GW added in just the past two and a half years. He further highlighted the significant reduction in the cost of non-fossil electricity, which had fallen from ₹11 per unit in 2012-13 to just ₹2.60 per unit today, owing to large-scale production. These developments, he said, demonstrated India’s growing strength in renewable energy and the opportunities available to expand its use in agriculture.
Citing a study by The Energy and Resources Institute (TERI), Union Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi said that, of India’s 116 million hectares of agricultural land, 47.5 million hectares – approximately 30 per cent – were technically suitable for AgriVoltaics. Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka and Uttar Pradesh together accounted for 50 per cent of this suitable land. He emphasised that if AgriVoltaics installations were established on just 10 per cent of this suitable area, India could meet its entire projected electricity demand up to 2050 through this approach alone. In addition to generating electricity, the technology had also been found to increase crop yields by 10 to 20 per cent. He highlighted the potential of AgriVoltaics to support the country’s long-term energy requirements while allowing agricultural land to continue producing crops, thereby creating a dual benefit for farmers and the wider economy.
Shri Joshi stated that, under the PM-KUSUM scheme, 30 lakh (3 million) agricultural pumps had so far been connected to solar energy. This had relieved farmers of the risks and difficulties associated with irrigating their fields at night while enabling them to access uninterrupted electricity during the day. He announced that the government would soon launch the world’s most ambitious AgriVoltaics programme under the next phase of PM-KUSUM. According to studies, the sector had the potential to generate approximately 3.32 lakh full-time local jobs. These employment opportunities would help rural youth find work in their own communities, reducing the need to migrate to district headquarters or major cities in search of livelihoods. The initiative, he said, could thus contribute to both the expansion of renewable energy and the creation of sustainable rural employment.
The inaugural session was attended by several distinguished dignitaries on the dais, including Union Minister of State for New and Renewable Energy Shri Shripad Yesso Naik; Dr Jasper Wieck, Ambassador of Germany to India and Bhutan; Shri Santosh Kumar Sarangi, Secretary, Ministry of New and Renewable Energy; Shri Atish Chandra, Secretary, Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare; Dr Mangi Lal Jat, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education and Director General of the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR); and Shri Ashish Khanna, Director General of the International Solar Alliance (ISA).
During the inaugural session, important technical tools and communication materials related to AgriVoltaics were also formally released and launched. These resources are intended to help farmers and other stakeholders make informed and precise decisions at the field level, supporting the practical implementation of AgriVoltaics and enabling more effective integration of agricultural activities with solar energy generation.

title: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare to Launch ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan – Rabi 2026’ tomorrow; Campaign to Continue Till 30 November
subtitle:
Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan to launch the campaign from Karnal, Haryana

Khet Bachao Abhiyan – Rabi 2026’ to Promote Balanced Fertilizer Use, Crop Diversification and Sustainable Farming Practices

Campaign to Organize Farmers’ Conferences, Kisan Chaupals, Training Sessions and Field Demonstrations Across All Administrative Levels
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 OCT 2026 6:56PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare will launch the nationwide ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan- Rabi 2026’ from 22 October to 30 November 2026 to promote sustainable agriculture, improve soil health and encourage the judicious use of agricultural resources. Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Union Minister of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, will launch the campaign from Karnal, Haryana.
The campaign aims to create awareness among farmers about the balanced and judicious use of fertilizers and other agricultural inputs based on soil testing. It will promote crop diversification through oilseed, pulse and horticulture missions, encourage the effective utilization of fallow fields after paddy harvesting and promote proper crop residue management. The campaign will also focus on training farmers in the appropriate use of organic and bio-based agricultural products and promoting natural farming through awareness programmes, training sessions and field demonstrations. In addition, it will emphasize water conservation, rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge, while encouraging sustainable agricultural practices to conserve natural resources and ensure the long-term sustainability of agriculture.
The campaign will focus on improving soil health, promoting the balanced use of fertilizers and other agricultural inputs, enhancing water-use efficiency, and encouraging the adoption of resource-efficient and climate-resilient farming practices. Special emphasis will be placed on creating awareness about the appropriate use of fertilizers, including green ammonia, and biological products; water conservation; crop diversification and intercropping with suitable crops and varieties; efficient utilization of rice fallows; natural farming; and integrated farming systems. Capacity building, farm mechanization and field demonstrations of improved technologies, including regenerative agriculture practices, will also form key components of the campaign.
Key themes will include crop residue management, integrated pest management, soil health management, climate-resilient agriculture, promotion of oilseeds and pulses, and seed distribution. The campaign will also facilitate the creation of Farmer IDs, promote awareness about crop insurance under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), expand coverage under the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme through saturation efforts, and disseminate information about the benefits and opportunities arising from trade agreements.
As part of the campaign, awareness programmes, farmers’ conferences, Kisan Chaupals, training sessions and field demonstrations will be organized at the State, district, block and Gram Panchayat levels. State Agriculture Departments, Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), ICAR institutes, State Agricultural Universities and Agricultural Technology Management Agencies (ATMA) will collaborate to ensure the active participation of agricultural scientists, ATMA functionaries, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), cooperatives, Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and progressive farmers. Publicity through local-language materials, radio, Doordarshan, social media and other IEC activities will further strengthen outreach and ensure wider dissemination of information among farmers.
The campaign targets reaching approximately one crore participants through ATMA and ICAR and total of 4,150 teams involving KVKs and ATMA are envisaged, with more than 12,000 scientists and ATMA functionaries expected to contribute to the campaign.
The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare will coordinate with State Governments, ICAR institutions and other stakeholders to ensure effective implementation and regular monitoring of the campaign, with particular emphasis on farmers’ participation and the adoption of sustainable agricultural practices.
Through the ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’, the Government seeks to strengthen soil and water conservation, promote efficient and cost-effective farming practices, improve agricultural sustainability and contribute to the long-term prosperity of farmers and the vision of Viksit Bharat.

title: DARE/ICAR Undertakes Nearly 4,000 Cleanliness Drives under Swachhata Special Campaign 6.0
subtitle:
Nearly 1.3 Lakh Square Feet of Space Freed under DARE/ICAR’s Swachhata Special Campaign 6.0 

DARE/ICAR Promotes Cleanliness, Waste Management and Sustainable Practices across Its Nationwide Network
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 OCT 2026 1:33PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), along with its 114 institutes, Regional Centres, Agricultural Technology Application Research Institutes (ATARIs) and Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), is participating in the month-long Swachhata Special Campaign 6 from 2nd to 31st October 2026.
Earlier, on 2nd October 2026, DARE/ICAR launched Swachhata Special Campaign 6.0 with cleanliness drives across its establishments nationwide. Officials of ICAR Headquarters participated in the drive at the National Agricultural Science Complex (NASC), Pusa, New Delhi. The initiative reflects a collective commitment to cleaner workplaces, greater public participation and a culture of sustained cleanliness, reinforcing the spirit of Swachhata. A floral tribute was also paid to Mahatma Gandhi on his birth anniversary.
Key highlights of Swachhata Special Campaign 6
Key highlights of Swachhata Special Campaign 6 across establishments include the organization of nearly 4,000 cleanliness campaigns, clearance of approximately 1.3 lakh square feet of space, and generation of around ₹10 lakh in revenue through the disposal of electronic and non-electronic scrap. Efforts are also underway to clear pending matters. Activities include cleanliness drives and Shramdaan in institutional premises, villages, roads and public spaces; Special Gram Sabhas, Swachhata Sabhas and awareness programmes on sanitation, hygiene, waste management and community responsibility; plogging and removal of litter; plantation and greening of Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs), including initiatives under “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam”; distribution and placement of dustbins; recognition of Safai Mitras, sanitation workers and volunteers; and beautification of cleaned spaces with before-and-after documentation. Other initiatives include sustainable waste management practices, such as vermicomposting of water hyacinth, and the review and weeding out of old files for appropriate disposal and records management.
Key outcomes of the
Swachhata Special Campaign 6
The key outcomes of the campaign include strengthened community participation and collective responsibility for cleanliness and sanitation; improved cleanliness of selected institutional and public spaces, documented through before-and-after photographs; and greater awareness of responsible waste disposal through dustbin distribution, waste collection and awareness programmes. The campaign also integrated cleanliness with environmental sustainability through plantation and greening of cleaned areas, recognized the contributions of Safai Mitras, sanitation workers and volunteers, and promoted sustainable practices such as vermicomposting of water hyacinth and the appropriate review and weeding out of old files.
Some of the major highlights of the campaign from DARE/ICAR Institutes are as follows:
ICAR–Central Coastal Agricultural Research Institute :
In ICAR–Central Coastal Agricultural Research Institute (ICAR–CCARI), highlight of the occasion was the Shramik Samman, wherein the Union Minister for Agriculture & Farmers Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan felicitated Safai Mitras of ICAR–CCARI with shawls, bouquets and gifts, as a mark of appreciation for the dedicated services of all Safai Mitras who work throughout the year to maintain a clean and hygienic campus. The programme highlighted the spirit of Swachhata, Seva and Shramik Samman, recognising the invaluable contribution of Safai Mitras towards a cleaner and healthier environment.
ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute (ICAR-IARI), New Delhi
:
The ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute (ICAR-IARI), New Delhi, observed Swachh Bharat Diwas on 2nd October 2026 under the theme “Swachhta Mein Sahbhag – Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat”, with a series of cleanliness activities across the Institute and a call for sustained participation towards maintaining a clean and healthy institutional environment. In his address, Secretary (DARE) & DG (ICAR), Dr. Mangi Lal Jat, appreciated the cleanliness drive undertaken by ICAR-IARI and called for making Swachhata a year-round activity, with cleanliness programmes being undertaken in a team-based manner. He emphasised that cleanliness and a better workplace environment contribute to the overall well-being of employees and support the advancement of science and the health of people. The importance of team building and creating a positive workplace environment was highlighted, noting its relevance to both institutional functioning and mental well-being. The importance of nurturing students for their holistic development was emphasized, enabling them to grow as responsible professionals and future contributors to science and society. As part of the programme, prizes were distributed to the winners of the painting competition organised by the Post Graduate School Students’ Union, ICAR-IARI, during the Swachhata Abhiyaan. The competition provided students an opportunity to express their ideas on cleanliness and environmental responsibility through art.
ICAR Institutes and establishments have promoted the principles of Reduce, Reuse and Recycle through activities such as Waste to Art, plastic-free initiatives and creative utilisation of waste materials. Emphasis has also been placed on converting waste into useful and aesthetically meaningful products, promoting awareness on responsible waste management and reinforcing the message that waste can be transformed into a resource.  As part of the cleanliness drive, non-degradable plastic waste, garbage and unwanted weeds were collected and removed from the premises. The activity helped improve the cleanliness and overall appearance of the campus. The participants were also sensitized and made aware of the importance of maintaining a clean and plastic-free campus and encouraged to contribute towards sustainable cleanliness practices.
Under
Swachhata Special Campaign 6,
DARE/ ICAR
are continuously working on raising awareness about hygiene among students for their better health.
Our present motto is fostering awareness of civic duties and cultivating corresponding habits for a healthy society. Raising of public awareness and promoting the campaign on a large scale is our goal. Some glimpses at
ICAR Research Complex For Eastern Region, Patna, Bihar
are shown below.
ICAR-Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture, Hyderabad, Telangana:
in ICAR-CRIDA appearance of the premises are being enhanced along with protection against harmful insects for people visiting or working in the fields. The cleanliness drive is aimed to maintain a clean, hygienic, and environmentally friendly atmosphere within the premises and to create awareness about the importance of cleanliness in agricultural research institutions. Special attention is being given to cleaning the farm surroundings, removing unwanted vegetation, collecting litter and waste materials, and maintaining cleanliness along internal pathways, open spaces, and other common areas. DARE/ ICAR highlights the role of cleanliness in improving workplace efficiency, ensuring the safety of farm personnel, and maintaining the overall appearance of the premises.
Before Swachhata                                           After Swachhata
In
ICAR-CCARI, Goa
, special activity was undertaken for scrap identification from field units to institutionalize Swachhata and minimize pendency by identifying unserviceable and obsolete items for proper disposal. As part of ongoing campaign, a special drive was conducted for the identification of scrap material from guest houses. The scrap like metal items 70 kg, MCB panels 200 kg, fencing wire 100 kg and plastic items 20 kg were identified for disposal. These items were catalogued for further processing under the approved disposal mechanism.
Under Special Campaign 6.0, cleanliness and upkeep of the plantation area at
ICAR–Mahatma Gandhi Integrated Farming Research Institute, Motihari, Bihar,
were taken up. The activity covered banana plantation rows and adjoining green spaces, with attention to overgrown weeds, unwanted vegetation and scattered litter. Regular removal of such growth and proper waste disposal are essential to keep plantation areas clean, accessible and well maintained. Key focus was plantation-row maintenance; weed and vegetation management; litter clearance and routine sanitation of institutional green spaces.
ICAR-National Bureau of Soil Survey and Land Use Planning, Nagpur
Laboratory waste was collected from various divisions/ sections of the institute and kept in secure location for safe disposal and auction.
ICAR-Central Island Agricultural Research Institute
A cleanliness drive was conducted at the Animal Feed Processing Unit of ICAR–CIARI, Sri Vijaya Puram. The activity involved removing accumulated dry leaves, debris, and unwanted vegetation from the roof to maintain cleanliness, ensure proper drainage, and promote regular maintenance of institutional infrastructure under the Swachhata initiative.
Environment-friendly biological waste management activities were undertaken in the cattle, buffalo, goat and pig units of the institute, covering a total of 213 animals (22 cattle, 14 buffaloes, 105 goats and 72 pigs). The livestock sheds were cleaned using a high-pressure jet washer to maintain hygienic housing conditions. The wastewater generated during shed cleaning was collected and reused for irrigation of fodder plots, promoting water conservation and resource recycling. Livestock urine was collected and utilized for fodder irrigation to facilitate nutrient recycling. Animal dung from all livestock units was collected and transported to the vermicompost unit for conversion into organic manure. These activities promote efficient utilization of biological wastes, reduce indiscriminate waste disposal, conserve water and nutrients, and support sustainable livestock farming and fodder production. Thus, the initiative represents an integrated, environment-friendly approach to livestock waste management and a circular bio-resource utilization system.
ICAR-IIFSR, Modipuram, Meerut
The cleanliness drive involved collecting, organizing, and loading dry garden waste into a cart for disposal. The collected waste included dry leaves and large palm fronds, helping to maintain cleanliness in the park and the surrounding areas of the Institute.
ICAR-Research Complex for NEH Region, Umiam, Meghalaya
As theme of this year’s campaign was disposing of electronic waste, efforts were made to collect, segregate and dispose these items to authorised recyclers, refurbishers and developers for earning maximum revenue.
ICAR-National Meat Research Institute, Hyderabad
For wider dissemination and outreach, ICAR Headquarters has issued Press releases on activities undertaken under the campaign, while ICAR institutes and establishments have publicized their activities through local print media, banners and other communication channels. At both Headquarters and institutional levels, the campaign and its activities are also being disseminated through social media platforms, including Facebook, X and Instagram, thereby extending the message of Swachhata beyond the ICAR network to wider and more diverse audiences, particularly digitally engaged audiences and the younger generation.

title: CCO's SUVIKALP Initiative Advances Sustainable Mine Repurposing, Receives SKOCH Gold Award 2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 OCT 2026 12:47PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Coal Controller Organisation (CCO), under the Ministry of Coal, has undertaken initiatives to promote scientific mine closure and sustainable repurposing of post-mining land.
CCO has developed SUVIKALP, an in-house Mine Repurposing Tool, to assist stakeholders in selecting suitable mine repurposing projects through a structured and data-driven decision-making process. The tool evaluates and ranks repurposing projects based on multiple technical, environmental, social and economic criteria.
Once a suitable project is identified, users can explore implementation pathways through PRISM (Post-Mining Repurposing Implementation Strategy Model). PRISM provides project concepts, implementation approaches, case studies, sample Detailed Project Reports (DPRs), tender documents and information on agencies working in similar sectors.
The innovation and utility of SUVIKALP received national recognition through the SKOCH Gold Award 2026 under the category
“Digital Operational Efficiency
– Data Driven Decision Making
”
on 26 September 2026. The SKOCH Awards recognise excellence in governance, technology, innovation and transformational initiatives delivering public value.
CCO has also undertaken the SUVIKALP Samvaad Webinar Series as a structured knowledge-sharing and capacity-building initiative to support informed decision-making on mine closure and sustainable repurposing. The national webinar series brought together coal companies, government officials, technical experts, academic institutions and other stakeholders to share practical solutions, innovative models and best practices related to post-mining land use.
A total of 12 thematic webinars were conducted under the series, covering the RECLAIM and L.I.V.E.S. frameworks, SUVIKALP Mine Repurposing Tool, PMU establishment, community engagement, tourism and destination development, livelihood opportunities, financing mechanisms, innovative uses of abandoned mine voids, and national and international experiences of mine transition.
The series has strengthened the institutional understanding of coal companies on the multidimensional aspects of mine closure, moving beyond regulatory compliance towards environmental restoration, livelihood generation, community development and economic diversification. Expert-led deliberations and knowledge exchange have provided practical insights and scalable approaches for planning and implementing sustainable repurposing projects.
The initiatives support the Ministry of Coal's vision of transforming closed coal mines into productive assets and enabling sustainable regional development.

title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal to Visit Germany and the Netherlands to Strengthen Trade, Investment and Industrial Cooperation
subtitle:
India to Explore New Opportunities for Industrial and Technological Collaboration with Germany and the Netherlands

Around 100 Businesses and Startups to Accompany Shri Piyush Goyal on Visit to Germany and the Netherlands
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 OCT 2026 5:38PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal will undertake an official visit to Germany (22–24 October 2026) and the Netherlands (24–27 October 2026) to deepen strategic economic partnerships, expand bilateral trade and advance industrial and technological collaboration.
During the Berlin leg of the visit, Shri Piyush Goyal will participate in the Berlin Global Dialogue, engaging with international policymakers and global business leaders to highlight India’s macroeconomic stability, manufacturing capabilities and pivotal role in building resilient global supply chains. On the sidelines of the summit, the Minister will hold high-level bilateral meetings with the German Federal Minister for Economic Affairs and Energy (BMWE) and the Economic and Financial Policy Advisor and G7/G20 Sherpa at the Federal Chancellery of Germany. The meetings will focus on strengthening bilateral trade and investment corridors, accelerating technological and industrial cooperation in advanced engineering, green mobility and clean technology, and exploring market access and investment avenues arising from the ongoing India–EU Free Trade Agreement (FTA) negotiations.
Proceeding to the Netherlands, Shri Piyush Goyal will lead comprehensive government-to-government (G2G) engagements in The Hague, holding bilateral ministerial meetings with the Minister of Economic Affairs and Climate and the Minister for Foreign Trade and Development Cooperation to explore expanded trade channels and green transition initiatives. The visit will also encompass key discussions with the King’s Commissioner of North Holland and members of the Dutch Parliament’s committees on foreign trade and European affairs.
Shri Piyush Goyal will be accompanied by around 100 businesses and startups in Germany and the Netherlands. The Indian business delegation accompanying the Minister will have a parallel programme in Berlin, which includes sectoral roundtables with German CEOs and Indian business delegates. The roundtables will cover automotive, advanced manufacturing, infrastructure and energy; information technology, artificial intelligence and services; agri-food, consumer goods and textiles; and healthcare, pharmaceuticals and wellness. The delegation will also participate in an India–Germany Investment Roundtable with Germany Trade & Invest (GTAI) on investing and establishing operations in Germany. It will also interact with German innovation and research institutions and think tanks on industrial transformation, deeptech, microelectronics, skills development, and India–Germany trade, investment and resilient supply chains.
The Indian business delegation will also visit the Port of Rotterdam on 25 October 2026 to see the port’s logistics and supply chain infrastructure. On 26 October 2026, Shri Piyush Goyal will address businesses from both countries, along with the Dutch Minister for Foreign Trade and Development Cooperation, at the India–Netherlands Business Forum in The Hague. The Business Forum will be followed by six parallel sectoral roundtables and B2B networking, covering agri-food and food processing; high technology and innovation; sustainability and renewable energy; logistics and supply chain connectivity; manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, textiles and engineering goods; and services and allied sectors.

title: Hon’ble President of India Smt. Droupadi Murmu presents 65th National Exhibition of Art and 3rd Print Biennale India awards to artists, celebrating India’s rich artistic heritage and contemporary creativity
subtitle: Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat graces the event organised by Lalit Kala Akademi
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 OCT 2026 7:01PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Hon’ble President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, today graced the award   ceremony of the 65th National Exhibition of Art and the 3rd Print Biennale India 2026, organised by the Lalit Kala Akademi under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi. Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister of Culture and Tourism and Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, were present on the occasion, along with senior officials, artists and members of the cultural fraternity.
The award ceremony recognised the outstanding contributions of artists to India’s rich cultural heritage and contemporary visual arts, with awards presented to selected artists as part of the 65th National Exhibition of Art and the 3rd Print Biennale India 2026.
The Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, welcomed the Hon’ble President and presented her with a Gond painting as a token of gratitude, reflecting the richness of India’s indigenous artistic traditions. A special film showcasing the journey of the Lalit Kala Akademi and the evolution of the National Exhibition of Art since its inception in 1955 was also screened on the occasion.
Addressing the gathering, the Hon’ble President, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, highlighted India’s rich and diverse artistic heritage, describing art as a mirror of the country’s culture, traditions and civilisational journey. She emphasised the importance of preserving traditional art forms and highlighted printmaking as a significant tradition of artistic expression.
The Hon’ble President also highlighted the role of exhibitions and biennales in encouraging dialogue and the exchange of ideas among artists. She appreciated the efforts of the Ministry of Culture in creating opportunities for the promotion and wider reach of artworks and integrating artists into the creative economy.
Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, appreciated the Lalit Kala Akademi for providing a national platform for artists to showcase their work and celebrate India’s artistic diversity. He highlighted the distinctive vision and creative expression reflected in every artwork, representing the artist’s unique perspective and imagination. He emphasised that this diversity of artistic expression enriches the world of art and strengthens India’s vibrant creative traditions.
Drawing on his experience of witnessing printmaking practices during the inauguration of the Print Biennale, the Union Minister highlighted the significance of printmaking as a medium that combines technical expertise with artistic innovation. He noted that platforms such as the National Exhibition of Art and the Print Biennale support artistic exchange, strengthen international connections and enhance the global visibility of Indian art.
Linking India’s cultural growth with the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047, Shri Shekhawat underscored the importance of Sanskriti Samriddhi and Indian creativity in the country’s development journey. He also highlighted the integration of artwork sales into the programme as an important step towards expanding opportunities for artists, strengthening their livelihoods and advancing India’s creative economy.
In his address, Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, traced the journey of the Lalit Kala Akademi since its establishment in 1954 and the evolution of the National Exhibition of Art, which began at Jaipur House in 1955 with approximately 1,200 entries.
Highlighting the scale of the 65th National Exhibition of Art, he noted that this year's edition received 6,175 artworks from 2,495 artists representing 27 States and Union Territories. A total of 270 artworks were selected for exhibition, and 20 artists were chosen for the Awards.
Shri Aggarwal also highlighted the importance of the Print Biennale in promoting printmaking, encouraging experimentation and facilitating interaction between Indian and international artists. He emphasised the Akademi’s continued efforts to expand public engagement with art, nurture emerging talent and create opportunities for artists to connect with wider audiences.
The Ministry of Culture will organise India Biennale 2026 from December 4, 2026, to March 21, 2027, across monuments and heritage sites in Delhi. The initiative will provide a platform for artistic expression and engagement with India’s cultural heritage, bringing contemporary creativity into dialogue with the country’s historic spaces.
The Biennale will further strengthen opportunities for artists to showcase their work, promote creative exchange and enhance public engagement with art and heritage.
The award ceremony reaffirmed the importance of preserving India’s diverse artistic traditions while encouraging contemporary creativity, wider recognition for artists and the integration of art into the country’s cultural and creative economy.

These operations underscore the scale and varied routes of synthetic drug trafficking, spanning inter-city transport networks, cross border and coastal corridors.
Through sustained intelligence-led enforcement, DRI remains committed to dismantling narcotics trafficking networks and preventing dangerous drugs from reaching illicit markets.

Union Home Secretary Shri Govind Mohan addressed a Press Conference in New Delhi today on Rashtriya Ekta Diwas
2026
and Bharat Parv
2026
celebrations to be held in Ekta Nagar, Gujarat.
Briefing the media, Union Home Secretary said that this year’s Ekta Parade will be more vibrant, diverse and attractive. The main function will commence on
31
st October
2026.
Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi will pay tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel at the ‘Statue of Unity’ in the morning. Ekta Parade will be held in the evening. The Parade will lay emphasis on the massive achievement of getting India rid of armed Naxalism in
2026.
Shri Govind Mohan said that the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations at Ekta Nagar have been envisioned keeping two purposes in mind. The first purpose is to bring to the attention of the nation, the extraordinary work being done by the Police forces, Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and Central Police Organisations (CPOs) of the country. The second purpose is to invite the people from all parts of the country to witness and enjoy the local surroundings of Ekta Nagar, along with the largest statue in the world of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. He said that several other attractions have been created around Ekta Nagar, which has now emerged as one of the most prominent and most attractive tourist destinations in the country.
Union Home Secretary said that during the Ekta Diwas parade, we will be celebrating the end of armed Naxalism in the country. He said this will be done through three different and unique performances:
This year’s parade contingents will include State Police forces and CAPFs who have been at the forefront of the country’s fight against armed Naxalism. During the passage of each of these contingents before the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on
31
st October,
2026

126

5,000
people from these
126

150

15

date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 OCT 2026 1:41PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today paid tribute to the police personnel who laid down their lives in the line of duty at the National Police Memorial in New Delhi on the occasion of Police Commemoration Day and addressed the ceremony. On this occasion, Union Home Minister flagged off a nationwide motorcycle rally organised around the message “Fight against Drugs.” The Police Commemoration Day ceremony was attended by Members of Parliament Shri Krishna Prasad Tenneti and Shri Rajiv Kumar; Union Home Secretary Shri Govind Mohan; Director of the Intelligence Bureau Shri Mahesh Dixit; Director General of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police Shri Shatrujeet Kapoor; the Directors General of other Central Armed Police Forces; and several senior officers.
Addressing the gathering, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said they had assembled at the National Police Memorial to pay homage to the brave police personnel who had made the supreme sacrifice in service of the nation from Independence to the present day. He said that nearly eight decades after Independence, India stands today in a position of honour and respect in the world. The foundation of this achievement lies in the sacrifices of our brave personnel. No one can even imagine where we would stand today if these personnel had not made the supreme sacrifice to safeguard the country’s internal security and protect its borders.
Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that 2026 is an extremely significant year for the Indian police. On March 31, 2026, the country achieved freedom from Naxalism, which had plagued India for decades. From 1981 to March 2026, the country endured numerous hardships due to Naxalism. During this period, many brave security personnel and innocent civilians lost their lives. More than 3,600 security personnel were martyred, and nearly 13,700 innocent civilians also lost their lives. Union Home Minister said he wanted to convey to the families of the martyred personnel that as the country moves forward on the path of development after overcoming this five-decade-old problem, the sacrifices of these 3,600 personnel form the foundation of this progress. Addressing the families of the martyrs, the Home Minister said that while their loss could never be compensated, the entire nation of 1.4 billion citizens remains grateful for the dedication and sacrifice of their families.
Recalling the history of Police Commemoration Day, Shri Amit Shah said that on October 21, 1959, in the remote and inhospitable Hot Springs region of Ladakh, 10 CRPF personnel laid down their lives while bravely resisting an attack by Chinese troops. A study of the Hot Springs incident makes it clear that when the battle was decided in the high-altitude mountains, the outcome was almost certain. Yet, these immortal heroes remained steadfast in their resolve that not even an inch of the country’s land should fall into foreign hands, making the supreme sacrifice in the line of duty. Since then, October 21 has been observed every year as Police Commemoration Day. He said that the National Police Memorial, where they were gathered, was inaugurated in 2018 by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in honour of police personnel who had laid down their lives across the country. The objective behind establishing the memorial was to inspire future generations of police personnel to remain committed to their responsibilities and be prepared to make the supreme sacrifice while performing their duties. He added that the memorial has also become a place of reverence for citizens from across the country. Grateful citizens visit the site to pay tribute to 36,852 police personnel and express the nation's gratitude for their service and sacrifice.
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that among all government services, police service is one of the most challenging. Every citizen in the country celebrates festivals such as Raksha Bandhan, Holi, Diwali and Eid, but police personnel often have no holidays to celebrate these occasions. He said that while people celebrate festivals with their families, police personnel remain on duty, safeguarding internal security, managing traffic and ensuring public safety. Devoting the prime years of one’s life to the nation while staying away from one’s family is a great service to the country.
Shri Amit Shah said that there are numerous examples across the country of police personnel demonstrating extraordinary patience, restraint, discipline, courage and dedication, thereby strengthening the nation’s internal security. He said that police personnel constitute both the first and the last line of defence for internal security. He expressed his special gratitude to all personnel of the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) deployed along the borders and entrusted with security responsibilities within the country. Staying away from their families, these personnel remain vigilant and strengthen the nation’s internal security on every occasion, whether during elections, festivals, protests or border security duties. They remain constantly on duty to ensure the smooth functioning of the country. Whether it is safeguarding democracy or ensuring the smooth conduct of democratic processes, it is impossible to imagine these tasks being accomplished without the Central Armed Police Forces. Shri Shah said that India had succeeded in eliminating electoral violence in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, but electoral violence had continued in West Bengal for a long time. He said that during the recently concluded West Bengal Assembly elections, security personnel achieved a significant success by ensuring that the elections were completed without a single fatality. In doing so, the Central Armed Police Forces had established a new benchmark. He added that the entire country now recognises that electoral violence has been brought to an end in the nation.
Union Home Minister said that over the past few years, the country had faced several challenges, three of which had persisted for decades. He said that peace has now been established in all three major hotspots—Kashmir, the North-East and the areas affected by Left-Wing Extremism. An environment conducive to development has emerged in these regions, and they are now ready to compete with the rest of the country in terms of development. Shri Shah said that significant success had been achieved in curbing terrorism in Kashmir. Following several agreements and the surrender of arms by thousands of people, the entire North-East has moved forward on the path of peace. He added that police and Central Armed Police Forces personnel had achieved a major breakthrough in completely eliminating the five-decade-old Naxal problem, which had spread across several states. He specifically thanked the CRPF and its CoBRA Battalion for their contribution to the elimination of Naxalism and praised the bravery of the Chhattisgarh Police.
Shri Amit Shah said that the country has not yet become completely free of problems and that several challenges remain. He stated that the Union Ministry of Home Affairs has set a target to free the country from the drug menace by December 31, 2029, through a concerted fight against drugs over the remaining part of 2026 and the next three years—2027, 2028 and 2029. He described this as a very important goal for the nation. He said that drug abuse and trafficking undermine the future of coming generations, place an unnecessary burden on the economy and often provide financial support to organisations with anti-national intentions. Union Home Minister called upon police forces across the country to wholeheartedly join the efforts to implement the roadmap for a ‘
Nasha Mukt Bharat’
, formulated under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, and work towards safeguarding future generations.
The motorcycle rally flagged off by Home Minister today includes around 90 riders from various States and Union Territories (Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh and Delhi), Central Armed Police Forces (CRPF, CISF, BSF, SSB, ITBP and NSG), and certain central police organisations (RPF, NDRF and NIA). The rally is part of a nationwide campaign organised around the message “Fight against Drugs”, in which motorcycle riders from all States, Union Territories and Central Forces across the country will reach Ekta Nagar, Gujarat, to participate in the Ekta Parade-2026.

title: NFDC–NFAI to present a Four-Day Ritwik Ghatak Film Festival in Pune, offering a rare glimpse into the Filmmaker’s Diverse Cinematic Legacy
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 OCT 2026 6:13PM by PIB Mumbai
content:
: Mumbai, 21st October 2026
The NFDC–National Film Archive of India (NFDC–NFAI) will organise a four-day film festival,
“GHATAK: A RETROSPECTIVE”
, from October 22 to 25, 2026, at its auditorium on Law College Road, Pune. The retrospective will showcase 4K-restored feature films, rare 35mm prints, non-fiction documentaries, educational shorts and digitised fragments of incomplete works by iconic filmmaker Ritwik Ghatak. The festival offers film scholars, students and cinephiles an opportunity to explore the breadth of Ghatak’s cinematic contributions, including his directorial works and lesser-known projects across different creative roles.
The festival will open on October 22 with
Chinnamul
(1950), directed by Nemai Ghosh, in which Ghatak appeared as an actor. The film portrays the displacement of rural communities following Partition and offers an insight into an important phase of Ghatak’s early cinematic journey, before he emerged as a major directorial voice.
The programme brings together 4K-restored prints of Ghatak’s acclaimed feature films, including
Nagarik
(1952),
Ajantrik
(1958),
Bari Theke Paliye
(1959),
Meghe Dhaka Tara
(1960),
Komal Gandhar
(1961),
Subarnarekha
(1962),
Titash Ekti Nadir Naam
(1973) and
Jukti Takko Aar Gappo
(1974). It also features
Musafir
(1957), directed by Hrishikesh Mukherjee, for which Ghatak contributed to the screenplay, and
Madhumati
(1958), directed by Bimal Roy, for which he contributed to the story and screenplay. These Hindi films highlight the breadth of his creative contributions and place his work within the wider landscape of Indian cinema.
The retrospective also includes documentaries and short-form works such as
Bihar Ke Darshaniya Sthan
(1955),
Fear
(1965),
Rendezvous
(1965),
Nagarik Sanrakshan/Civil Defence
(1965),
My Lenin
(1970),
Scientists of Tomorrow
(1967),
Puruliar Chhau
(1970),
Adivasiyon Ka Jeevan
,
Yeh Kyun
(1970) and
Durbar Gati Padma
(1971). These works offer insights into Ghatak’s engagement with documentary filmmaking, cultural practices, public life and artistic expression beyond feature-length narratives.
Of particular archival significance are the incomplete works included in the programme:
Rounger Golam
,
Bagalar Banga Darshan
,
Kato Ajanare
(1959) and Ghatak’s incomplete biographical film on renowned sculptor Ramkinkar Baij. The retrospective will present surviving fragments of these incomplete and unrealised works, restored and digitised in 2K/4K under the National Film Heritage Mission (NFHM). Their public screening offers audiences a rare opportunity to encounter cinematic material that does not exist in the form of completed films. These fragments also underscore the role of film archives in preserving not only completed films but also incomplete and lesser-known works that contribute to a fuller understanding of a filmmaker’s creative journey.
The restoration of these films was undertaken under the National Film Heritage Mission, a flagship initiative of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India, dedicated to preserving the country’s audiovisual heritage. The meticulous 4K restorations drew upon original film elements preserved over several decades by NFDC–NFAI, along with valuable materials from the West Bengal State Film Archive. To ensure visual authenticity and fidelity to Ghatak’s original cinematic vision, the colour-grading process was supervised by National Award-winning cinematographer Shri Avik Mukhopadhyay, who lauded the restoration initiative.
For the detailed schedule, interested persons may write to
nfaifilmcircle@nfdcindia.com
or visit NFDC–NFAI’s social media platforms.

title: Law Commission of India to organise National Conference on ‘Co-operative Federalism and Law Reforms: National and State Perspectives’
subtitle:
Vice-President of India Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan to inaugurate the Conference

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice
Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal to grace the occasion

Two technical sessions to bring together State Law Commissions, jurists, legal scholars and policymakers for dialogue on collaborative law reform
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 OCT 2026 1:56PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The 23rd Law Commission of India is hosting a National Conference on “Co-operative Federalism and Law Reforms: National and State Perspectives” on 22 October 2026 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, bringing together representatives of State Law Commissions and other equivalent bodies, eminent jurists, former judges, legal scholars, policymakers and members of the Bar and academia from across the country.
The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, will inaugurate the Conference, in the presence of Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law & Justice.
The senior leadership of the 23rd Law Commission of India—Chairperson, Justice (Retd.) Dinesh Maheshwari; Member, Prof. D.P. Verma; and Member Secretary, Dr. Anju Rathi Rana—will also be present.
The Conference will deliberate on contemporary issues relating to law reforms, co-operative federalism, constitutional governance and institutional frameworks for the effective administration of justice. It seeks to strengthen coordination among States and institutions engaged in law reform, while respecting State autonomy and ensuring that reforms remain responsive to both national and regional requirements.
The theme draws from India’s constitutional distribution of law-making powers across the Union, State and Concurrent Lists in the Seventh Schedule. The Conference will consider how the Union and the States can work together on legal reform within this constitutional framework, and how coordination between the Law Commission of India, State Law Commissions and equivalent bodies can be strengthened.
The first technical session, “Reforms in Law: Needs and Methods”, will examine the need for continuous review and reform of laws in response to social, economic and technological change, as well as the methods and institutional processes through which such reform may be undertaken. The session will also consider justice-oriented and accessible legal reform; adaptive legislation and periodic statutory review; the role of India’s traditions of Nyaya, Kartavya and Lok Kalyan to develop context-sensitive reform; research-led law reform; and the relationship between law reform, social harmony and Viksit Bharat.
The second technical session, “Allocated Powers, Shared Goals: Drafting the Future with Collaborative Jurisprudence”, will examine law reform within a system of divided legislative powers, including avenues for greater consultation and coordination between national and State institutions while ensuring that State legislation remains responsive to local needs.
The Conference is intended to provide a forum for National and State experiences to inform a more coordinated approach to law reform, and for participating institutions to identify areas in which sustained consultation and cooperation can improve the process and implementation of legal reform.

title: National Institute for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (ni-msme) strengthens MSMEs through Capacity Building, Entrepreneurship Development and Digital Empowerment
subtitle: 11,032 executives from 150 countries trained through 550 international programmes; 17,672 programmes conducted in India benefiting 6,07,497 participants
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 OCT 2026 7:49PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Institute for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (ni-msme), an autonomous Institute under the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India, plays a significant role in promoting entrepreneurship, strengthening managerial capabilities and supporting the growth of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSME) across the country. Through special training programmes, research, consultancy, capacity building and institutional partnerships, the Institute contributes to building a competitive, skilled and innovation-oriented MSME ecosystem.
The institute accredited with “UTKRISHT / उत्कृष्ट” 3-Star Rating by the Capacity Building Commission (CBC). The 66 years old institute plays a pivotal role in promoting innovation, entrepreneurship, and capacity building for MSME development by fostering a pro-business environment. Over the decades, it has evolved to address the changing needs of entrepreneurs, policymakers, government institutions and industry stakeholders, with a focus on capacity building, sustainable enterprise development and enhanced competitiveness.
Legacy of Enterprise Development
The Institute was established in 1960 as the Central Industrial Extension Training Institute (CIETI) in New Delhi. It shifted to Hyderabad in 1962 and was registered as the Small Industry Extension Training Institute (SIET). Following the enactment of the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006, the Institute was renamed the National Institute for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (ni-msme) in 2007.
The Institute covers enterprise creation, finance, marketing, international trade, digital transformation, technology adoption and sustainable business practices, supporting employment generation, productivity and inclusive economic growth.
Key Achievements of ni-msme
International Training: Conducted 550 international programmes, training 11,032 executives from 150 countries.
National Training: Organised 17,672 programmes, benefiting 6,07,497 participants.
Skill Development: Conducted 6,840 programmes, training 2,10,062 youth.
MSME Cluster Development: Implemented 27 MSME cluster projects.
IPFC Services: Provided 235 services through Intellectual Property Facilitation Centres (IPFCs).
Research and Studies: Completed 962 research studies to support MSME development and policymaking.
Supporting Innovation and Emerging Enterprise Needs
As businesses increasingly adapt to digital technologies, changing market expectations and evolving production systems, ni-msme continues to engage with emerging areas of enterprise development. Its programmes and institutional activities encompass subjects such as digital marketing, e-commerce, artificial intelligence, technology-enabled manufacturing, intellectual property rights, green energy and sustainable enterprise practices. These areas are increasingly relevant to MSME seeking to improve operational efficiency, develop new products, expand their market reach and remain competitive.
In March 2026, the Institute organised a national conference on Digital Marketing, AI Automation and e-Commerce, followed by a national conference on Digital Enabled Factories with Industry 5.0, focusing on artificial intelligence, the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and cloud technologies. These engagements provided platforms for discussing the application of emerging technologies in enterprise development and manufacturing. Through such knowledge-sharing initiatives, ni-msme contributes to raising awareness of new business opportunities and encouraging MSME to explore technology-driven approaches to growth.
Success Stories Reflect ni-msme’s Transformational Impact:
(a)
Weaving New Markets: A Traditional Silk Enterprise Goes Digital
Mr. Mahankali Chandra Sekhar’sAmarchintha Handloom Weavers Producer Company Ltd., Wanaparthy, Telangana, is weaving a new success story through digital transformation.
In 2024–25, with support from NABARD, the company’s marketing executive underwent a five-day training programme at ni-msme, Ministry of MSME, followed by one year of handholding to strengthen digital branding and market outreach.
By leveraging Instagram, WhatsApp Business and Google Business Profile, the company secured a landmark ₹16 lakh order through Google, while its annual turnover surged to ₹2.8 crore. Amarchintha’s journey is a testament to how digital adoption can expand market access, empower traditional artisans and drive MSME growth.
(b) From Millets to Markets: A Woman Entrepreneur’s Growth Story
Smt. SunkishalaSwarupa, a woman entrepreneur from Shayampet, Telangana, transformed her millet food business through digital marketing. Under a NABARD-supported project implemented by ni-msme, Ministry of MSME, she underwent a five-day training programme on digital branding and marketing, followed by one year of handholding support.
By leveraging Instagram, Google My Business and Canva, she enhanced her online visibility, expanded her customer base and strengthened the promotion of her millet products.
The Impact:
10-fold growth in monthly turnover, from ₹20,000 to ₹2 lakh.
Employment created for local women.
Her journey showcases how digital empowerment can transform women-led enterprises and drive inclusive MSME growth.
Ni-msme: Empowering MSME, Enabling Growth
Through its sustained efforts in entrepreneurship development, capacity building, research and digital empowerment, ni-msme continues to strengthen India’s MSME ecosystem and foster inclusive economic growth. Its achievements in training lakhs of participants, supporting enterprise development and enabling success stories demonstrate its commitment to empowering entrepreneurs, enhancing competitiveness and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities. By equipping enterprises with the skills, knowledge and tools to adapt to a changing business environment, ni-msme remains a key contributor to building a self-reliant, innovative and globally competitive MSME sector in India.

title: India hosts Agrivoltaics World Conference 2026
subtitle:
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) hosts conference with support from Federal Ministry for the Environment, Climate Action, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety (BMUV), Germany and Conexio-PSE

Calls for transforming India's Annadatas into Urjadatas through innovation-driven agrivoltaics
ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 OCT 2026 6:08PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The 7th edition of the AgriVoltaics World Conference (AWC) 2026 commenced today at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, marking a definitive milestone in the country's efforts to integrate agriculture and renewable energy. This premier global summit is being hosted in the Global South for the first time in India, firmly reinforcing India's expanding stewardship in concurrently advancing global food security, energy self-reliance, and sustainable development.
The prestigious three-day conference is being hosted by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), with support from the Federal Ministry for the Environment, Climate Action, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety (BMUV), Germany, and organised in partnership with Conexio-PSE under the theme "Powering the Global South."
The conference embodies the foundational vision of "From Power to Empower" championed by Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. He noted that India's clean energy transition is actively redefining the agrarian paradigm, enabling farmers to transcend traditional boundaries as raw-food producers (
Annadatas
) and emerge as pioneering clean-energy producers (
Urjadatas
).Hon’ble Prime Minister emphasised that India’ clean energy transition has unlocked unprecedented avenues to expand rural entrepreneurial ecosystems, optimise financial models, and cultivate long-term economic resilience across the country and called upon international stakeholders, scientists, and industry leaders to collaboratively scale precision agrivoltaics solutions that multiply farmer incomes whilst accelerating the transition to clean energy.
The opening ceremony on Day 1 began with the welcome of dignitaries and lighting of the ceremonial lamp, followed by welcome and opening remarks by Shri Santosh K. Sarangi, Secretary, Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE). A conference video was screened, setting the context for the three-day gathering and its focus on “Powering the Global South.”
The opening ceremony programme included addresses by Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and Shri Pralhad Joshi, Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy, Education and Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, followed by a video message from Mr. Carsten Schneider, Federal Minister for Environment, Climate Action, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety, Germany. Special closing remarks from Dr. Jasper Wieck, Ambassador of Germany to India and Bhutan. Present on the occasion was Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, Minister of State for New & Renewable Energy and Power.
The formal launch segment featured three knowledge resources: the Decision-Making Tool developed by the India Agrivoltaics Alliance (IAA), the Book of Abstracts developed by the International Water Management Institute (IWMI), and the AgriPV Policy Handbook from MNRE.
The conference has brought together over 1200+ delegates, including 150+ foreign participants, comprising international experts, policymakers, researchers, industry leaders, innovators, start-ups and development partners. The event provides a platform for knowledge exchange, technology collaboration and South-South cooperation. The above participation demonstrates a highly integrated governance strategy to align energy self-reliance with agricultural security.
The event featured Comprehensive Ecosystem Integration with regard to Science, Policy, and Innovation. Under this, the programme includes a dedicated India Focus Track alongside two parallel scientific tracks. Discussions across the conference will address innovation, state leadership, crop productivity, policy frameworks, financing models, technology deployment, climate resilience and farmer-centric business models.
Furthermore, a dedicated startup and innovation platform – featuring an interactive AgriVoltaics Pitch Hub - is actively showcasing next-generation technological solutions, bridging the gap among clean-tech innovators, start-ups, venture capitalists, and global industry leaders.
Agrivoltaics offers a transformative opportunity to mitigate rural underemployment, foster local entrepreneurship, increase farmers’ incomes, protect crop microclimates, and secure sustainable livelihoods against the escalating vagaries of climate change through the dual use of land for food and clean energy.
